title: On-prem migration workflow factory and LTS channel adapter
creator: Marina Alvarez
description:
Goal: Deliver a reusable on-prem migration workflow factory and an LTS channel adapter that let Private (VPC/on-prem) customers perform safe, staged upgrades across heterogeneous clusters. This ticket covers the controller and CLI for composing migration plans (schema, config, binary, and data migrations), the concept of LTS channels for customers to opt into slower upgrade cadences, and rollout gate hooks (health checks, SLO validation, drift detection).

Scope:
- Define versioning semantics for Private releases and LTS channels (major.minor+channel tags).
- Implement a migration-plan DSL that can express ordered steps, parallelizable steps, pre/post checks, and compensating actions.
- Build a controller that executes migration plans with deterministic checkpoints and durable state so upgrades can resume after failures.
- Add rollout gate integrations: metrics-based hold/release, manual approval, timed rollouts, and automated rollback triggers.
- Provide a migration CLI for on-prem operators and a controller-side API for Console and automation.
- Produce integration tests and a synthetic canary harness that simulates multi-node upgrades with KV-cache priming and rolling kernel swaps.

Non-goals: Fully automated schema transformations (we will provide hooks for migration scripts authored by platform teams/customers). No changes to public REST API compatibility guarantees — API compatibility is validated but breaking changes must be opt-in per channel.
acceptance_criteria: Versioning: Documented LTS channel semantics and mapping to release artifacts (e.g., 1.18-lts, 1.19-stable) and automated artifact promotion paths.
Migration DSL: Completed spec and parser for migration plan files, with ability to express sequence, parallel groups, pre/post checks, and compensating (rollback) steps.
Controller: Stateful controller deployed in test clusters that can start, pause, resume, and abort migration plans and persist progress to an encrypted store.
Rollout gates: Metrics-based gate that checks latency, error-rate, and replication lag; gate can pause rollout and trigger automatic rollback when thresholds are violated.
CLI/API: Migration CLI that can validate and submit plans to the controller and an API endpoint for Console to visualize plan state and audit trail.

Testing: End-to-end integration tests and a canary harness demonstrating a rolling upgrade with no more than 2x baseline p99 latency during steady-state migrations and successful rollback on injected failure.
Docs: Runbook and operator guide covering performing upgrades, creating migration scripts, and dealing with partial failures.
Security: Secrets used by migration controller are KMS-backed and operations are logged to the audit sink per Private compliance requirements.
